newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tankers little changed.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tankers little changed.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were mainly little changed on Monday, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) remaining at about W55 for Middle East-west voyages, brokers said.
"There's not much change all round -- pretty typical for a Monday," one said.

Middle East-Japan VLCC trips were fixed at around W65, unchanged from Friday, while voyages to Singapore were at a steady W55. I can see Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) from the Gulf going up on solid demand," another broker said. "But there has been very little action on rates today."
In the West Africa-U.S. sector VLCCs were little changed at W62.5, with 80,000 tonners remaining at W130, while transatlantic VLCCs remained at W62.5.
Brokers continued to put inter-U.K./Cont trips at W107.5 for 80,000 tonners.

One-million-barrel cross-Med cargoes were fixed at W82.5-W85, up slightly from W82.5 on Friday, while 80,000 tonnes was fixed at W105 "or a little bit more if it's loading in Syria or the Black Sea," an Italian broker said.
Fuel oil, which firmed sharply last week, was one of the few sectors to rise markedly on Monday.
"We've had a lot of interest, perhaps even a bit more than before," one fuel oil broker said.

He put 25,000 tonne cargoes of cross-Med fuel oil at W190, against W175 on Friday and inter-U.K./Cont at up to W200, from W195 previously. "There's also been a good deal of interest in 50,000 tonnes," he said, adding that these were being fixed at around W150 UKC-Med.

In Caribs/U.S. Gulf, U.S. brokers put 70,000 tonnes at a slightly softer W162.5-W165. "There's a little less tonnage than on Friday. The market's rather date-driven right now. You might see W160 but not much less," one said.
